title: Registering a user
idea: `registerUser` is the controller that creates an account: it rejects duplicates, saves the user with a hashed password, and emails a verification link.

analogy.text: A club's front desk: it checks the name is free, issues a membership card, and posts a confirmation letter. The member gets a receipt without the PIN.
analogy.breaks: A desk can undo steps; a failed email leaves the user saved.

points: `findOne` with `$or` finds a user who already has this username or email.
The email link holds the raw token; the database holds its hash and expiry.
One `save` writes the user, and the pre-save hook hashes the password.
The reply selects fields: password, refresh token and verification fields stay out.

steps.caption: Ada posts a username, email and password to `POST /api/v1/auth/register`.
`findOne` looks for a user with that username or email. None exists, so the request goes on.
A new user gets a token: its hash and expiry go on the document. `save` also hashes the password.
`sendEmail` mails a link that carries the raw token. The database never holds the raw token.
The reply is `201` with the user, minus the password and token fields.
A second request arrives with the same email.
`findOne` finds Ada's row. The controller throws `ApiError` 409: nothing is saved and no email goes out.
The error handler sends the 409 as JSON with `success: false`.

code.title: registerUser
code.caption: The last block is `src/controllers/auth.controllers.js`; the rest is earlier lessons, condensed. Press Run for real MongoDB output.

walk.text: Earlier lessons, condensed: error and reply classes, a mail stand-in, and the `User` model.
Read the fields. A username or email already in use ends with `409`.
Make a token. Store its hash and expiry. One `save` also hashes the password.
The link carries the raw token. If `sendEmail` rejects, the error leaves the controller.
Read the user back without secret fields, then reply `201` through `ApiResponse`.
A real request, then checks on the reply, the email and the database.
Repeat the request, then send nothing. Duplicates get `409`; missing fields get `500` for now.

pitfalls: Pick fields from `req.body`; passing it whole lets a client set `isEmailVerified: true`.
A failed email leaves a saved, unverified user; a later resend route covers it.
In production, build the link from fixed configuration: `req.get('host')` comes from the client.

quiz.q: With the register `User` model, what does this print?
quiz.why: The model stores the hash, not the raw token. `lowercase` runs when the value is set, and `isEmailVerified` defaults to `false`.

takeaway: Check, save with hashes, email the raw token, reply without secrets.

starters: Why store a hash of the token instead of the token itself?
What should happen if `sendEmail` fails after the user is saved?
Why does the controller read the user back before replying?
